query: What are 'sole possession' records, and must they be released to a student under FERPA?
gold_answer: 'Sole possession' records are letters or notes about a student kept in an employee's personal files and not shared with anyone else. They are not part of the education record, so they are not required to be released to a student under FERPA access rules.

query: What is the purpose of the policy on Morningside campus display cases?
gold_answer: It gives guidance on assigning display cases, keeping them aesthetically consistent and of good quality, the materials used to build them, and the obligation to keep posted materials current. It covers display cases along College Walk and also addresses cost issues.

query: Who gives final approval for instructional appointments of non-instructional officers for courses offered on the Morningside campus?
gold_answer: The Vice Provost for Academic Administration gives final approval for courses offered on the Morningside campus. For courses at the Medical Center, the Office of Faculty Affairs exercises that responsibility.

query: Where can a person obtain a printed copy of Columbia's annual security report?
gold_answer: Printed copies are available at the Public Safety offices on both the Morningside and Medical Center campuses. The report can also be requested by mail from the Campus Crime Report office at the Department of Public Safety.

query: What does the College Tuition Scholarship pay for eligible dependent children of full-time officers?
gold_answer: It pays 50% of a student's undergraduate tuition at accredited higher education institutions outside Columbia, up to an annually defined limit, for up to eight semesters or the equivalent number of trimesters or quarters.

query: Why does the University ban hoverboards on campus, and who enforces the ban?
gold_answer: The ban responds to Consumer Product Safety Commission reports of fire hazards from the lithium-ion batteries and the lack of safety standards for these devices. The Department of Public Safety enforces it, and the Vice President for Public Safety is the responsible officer.
expected_policy: Use of Hoverboards on University Campus and Property

query: When should a request to telecommute generally not be contemplated?
gold_answer: Requests generally should not be contemplated when the job requires physical presence (for example supervising other employees), efficiency suffers when the employee is absent, performance evaluations do not show sustained high performance, productivity is problematic, the employee needs close supervision, or the employee has less than six months of service in the unit.

query: How long must regular non-academic position vacancies be posted in TalentLink?
gold_answer: They must be posted for a minimum of five business days. Positions at grade levels 14 / 106 and above must be posted for at least fourteen calendar days, and all postings must include salary ranges.

query: By when must an employee complete Section I of the Form I-9?
gold_answer: Employees must complete Section I of the I-9 Form on or before their first day of employment.

query: How often are employees in the Protection of Minors at Columbia program background checked?
gold_answer: They are background checked every two years.

query: What is the maximum regularly scheduled work week for an employee holding a part-time job who is also hired part-time by another department?
gold_answer: The combined regularly scheduled work week may not exceed 35 hours, and the additional work must be authorized by the unit where the employee was initially hired.

query: Who may authorize an early closing of a location because of lack of climate control?
gold_answer: Vice Presidents, Deans, Human Resources Representatives and Departmental Administrators may authorize it, subject to prior review with HR Client Services and Labor Relations.
expected_policy: Closing Due to Lack of Climate Control

query: What is the maximum number of hours a variable hours officer may work in a rolling twelve-month period?
gold_answer: A variable hours officer is limited to 999 hours in a rolling 12-month period and should average fewer than 20 hours a week.

query: What must an employee obtain before returning from FMLA leave for a serious health condition?
gold_answer: The employee must obtain medical clearance from their health care provider, and the University may require additional clearance from a University-designated physician.

query: What happens to sick leave if an employee is hospitalized during vacation?
gold_answer: If the employee becomes seriously ill and is hospitalized during vacation and this is confirmed by documentation, the disability period is treated like any disability circumstance and the appropriate vacation time is restored.

query: How much paid medical leave are full-time Officers of Administration entitled to?
gold_answer: They are entitled to paid medical leave for up to six months during any rolling 12-month period when an extended absence is caused by illness or accident.

query: What should staff do until the Emergency Management Operations Team decides on the nature and extent of an emergency?
gold_answer: All management and staff should report to work as usual until the decision is made.
expected_policy: Establishing EssentialNon-essential Personnel in Case of a Campus Emergency

query: Are Flexible Work Arrangements considered medical accommodations?
gold_answer: No. FWAs are not medical accommodations, nor a substitute for requests such as FMLA or PFL. Medical accommodation questions go to the Office of Leave Management.

query: How close to a University building may a person smoke outdoors under the Smoking Policy?
gold_answer: Smoking is prohibited outdoors within 20 feet of all University buildings, including undergraduate housing. E-cigarettes and vaping devices are covered by the same prohibition.

query: What minimum general liability insurance must a commercial drone operator carry to fly on campus?
gold_answer: The operator must provide a certificate of insurance naming The Trustees of Columbia University as additional insured with a minimum of $5 million in general liability insurance written on an occurrence basis.
expected_policy: Use of Unmanned Aircraft Systems on University Campus and Property

query: What is the consequence of submitting incomplete or inaccurate information when establishing a new academic program?
gold_answer: It prevents the Office of the Registrar's final approval and the proper recording of the program in SIS, which can affect student registration services and eligibility for federal and state financial aid.
expected_policy: Central Administration of the University's Academic Programs

query: What withholding rate generally applies to honoraria paid to non-permanent residents through Candex, and how can a treaty exemption be claimed?
gold_answer: Payments not exempt from withholding are generally subject to 30% federal income tax withholding. To claim a tax treaty exemption, the payee must submit Form 8233 with any required supporting documents to Candex.
expected_policy: Policy for Making Payments With Candex

query: Is a Voluntary Leave of Absence a type of withdrawal, and who sets the detailed rules?
gold_answer: Yes, it is a type of Withdrawal that gives the student an exception from the continuous registration requirement. Each school articulates its own Voluntary Leave policies, and students should consult their school bulletin or Dean of Students.

query: What may the Dean of Students do when safety is an immediate concern during an Involuntary Leave of Absence process?
gold_answer: The DOS or designee may remove the student from campus pending the final decision. The student is given notice of the removal and later gets an opportunity to be heard and, if desired, to appeal.

query: Who is eligible for readmission under the Military Leave of Absence Policy?
gold_answer: U.S. military veterans who began their leave on or after August 14, 2008 and performed active duty service for more than 30 consecutive days with a discharge other than dishonorable or bad conduct. Cumulative military absence generally must not exceed five years.

query: How old can an expense be before petty cash may not be used to reimburse it?
gold_answer: Custodians should not reimburse expenses older than 120 days. Such expenses must be processed on an Expense Report.

query: How long is the grace period before tagged, likely abandoned bicycles are removed from campus bike racks?
gold_answer: After being tagged with a notice, bikes get a grace period of 21 days before removal and storage at the Department of Public Safety. Public Safety conducts bi-weekly inspections to identify likely abandoned bikes.

query: What training must undergraduate student organizations complete before programming events with alcohol?
gold_answer: Representatives must complete a formal training session on University programming with alcohol, offered three times each term by University Event Management with Columbia Health, Public Safety and CUEMS. Only students of legal drinking age may be authorized to program such events.
expected_policy: Alcohol Guidelines for Undergraduate Student Events

query: Which F&A rate applies when a research project is spread across multiple sites?
gold_answer: The On-Campus F&A Rate for the site with the preponderance of activity (more than 50%) applies to the entire project. For example, if most activity is on the Main Campus, the On-Campus Rate applies.
expected_policy: Application of Facilities and Administrative Cost Rate

query: How far in advance must a Section 98 caterer's permit application reach the State Liquor Authority?
gold_answer: The application must be received by the Liquor Authority at least 15 days before the event, and a menu must be submitted with it. The permit is valid for no more than 24 consecutive hours.
expected_policy: Alcohol Policy for Graduate Student, Faculty and Staff Events

query: What must a Recognized Student Group do before holding a barbecue on campus?
gold_answer: It must seek its Advisor's approval and submit a request to Event Management for an approved outdoor space location.

query: Who is responsible for classifying University Data under the Data Classification Policy?
gold_answer: The applicable Data Owner is responsible for evaluating and classifying the University Data under their responsibility. The policy's levels are Sensitive, Confidential, Internal and Public.

query: Which endpoints must be registered with the IT Custodian under the endpoints policy?
gold_answer: Endpoints that process, transmit or store PHI, endpoints handling University Data whose owner or related managers are primarily affiliated with CUIMC or the Columbia Health Care Component, and any endpoint used within the Columbia Health Care Component.
expected_policy: Registration And Protection Of Endpoints Policy

query: Who is responsible for documenting that directly charging an administrative or clerical salary to a federal project is appropriate?
gold_answer: Responsibility rests with both the Principal Investigator and the academic department, whether at the time of the transaction or later on audit.
expected_policy: Charging Administration and Clerical Salaries, Federal Grants and Contracts

query: What are the three components of the Information Security Program's mission?
gold_answer: The mission is to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of University Data. Confidentiality means access only by authorized users, integrity means accuracy and completeness, and availability means authorized users can access the data when needed.

query: Does the Acceptable Usage policy prohibit doxing and cyberstalking?
gold_answer: Yes. Users may not intimidate, harass, threaten or harm others, including through doxing, cyberbullying, deep fakes, cyberstalking, non-consensual image use or impersonation.
expected_policy: Acceptable Usage of Information Resources Policy

query: Who may be granted access to Columbia information resources under the Access Control and Log Management Policy?
gold_answer: Access is limited to faculty, staff, students and contractors who have been properly authorized to carry out legitimate business or academic tasks.
expected_policy: Information Resource Access Control and Log Management Policy

query: How must emails with patients containing PHI be transmitted, and what must the subject line include?
gold_answer: They must be sent in encrypted form on an Approved University Email System. The subject line must include #encrypt and must not include any PHI. Unencrypted email is allowed only at a patient's request after the patient completes the required step.

query: Who must install and maintain network, communications and telecommunications equipment and cabling?
gold_answer: CUIT or CUIMC IT must install and maintain them, either alone or in collaboration with NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital Information Technology.

query: What security control frameworks does the Information Security Risk Management Program draw on, and what factors guide control selection?
gold_answer: It selects elements from frameworks including ISO 27002. Controls are chosen based on the nature, feasibility and cost effectiveness of the controls for mitigating identified risks.

query: Which office serves as Incident Lead for a suspected compromise of PHI?
gold_answer: The Office of HIPAA Compliance serves as Incident Lead for any actual or suspected compromise of PHI. The applicable Information Security Office leads for other Sensitive Data.
expected_policy: Electronic Data Security Breach Reporting and Response Policy

query: How must Sensitive Data be sanitized before an information resource leaves the University?
gold_answer: It must be made fully unrecoverable, using CUIT or CUIMC IT data deletion software or disposal processes, approved destruction hardware (degaussing, shredding, pulverizing, melting), release to CUIT or CUIMC IT for destruction, or release to an approved vendor.
expected_policy: Sanitization and Disposal of Information Resources Policy

query: Which officer is responsible for heating, cooling, utilities, fire safety and elevator maintenance under the building services policy?
gold_answer: The Assistant Vice President for Plant Engineering and Utilities is responsible for those areas. The Assistant Vice President for Campus Operations handles general maintenance and repair of buildings and surrounding environs.

query: How quickly are mail meter requests processed by Administrative Mail?
gold_answer: Requests are processed within 24 business hours, and postage fees are charged to the applicable departmental account.

query: When are proctors required at events where attendees may include persons under 21?
gold_answer: Where under-21 attendees are possible, individuals must present double proof of age before being served alcohol (a valid Columbia ID may be the second proof), and such events require proctors as directed by the University.

query: After what time do New York City noise codes prohibit amplification, and when may limited amplification exceptions be made on campus?
gold_answer: NYC noise codes prohibit amplification after 10 p.m. University policy bars excessive amplification during business hours, with limited exceptions between 12 p.m. and 2 p.m. and 5 p.m. to 10 p.m. Amplification is not approved during reading or exam periods.

query: Where is data for the Operating Budget and Current Estimate collected?
gold_answer: It is collected in the Budgeting Tool module of FinSys, the University's financial web portal.

query: When will the Office of Institutional Equity handle a matter under the Title IX Grievance Process rather than the standard faculty and staff policy?
gold_answer: When the alleged conduct meets the narrow definitional and jurisdictional requirements of Title IX.

query: How does the Anti-Doxing and Online Harassment Policy define doxing?
gold_answer: Doxing is the electronic or physical publication of an individual's personal information (such as private email, phone number or home address) that intimidates, threatens or harasses the person or encourages additional harassment.

query: Whom does the Anti-Hazing Policy apply to, and what law does it help the University comply with?
gold_answer: It applies to all students, faculty and staff, covering conduct on or off campus including online activity. It supports compliance with the federal Stop Campus Hazing Act.

query: Who must be included among authorized signers on a University bank account?
gold_answer: Unless otherwise authorized in writing, signatories must be Columbia employees and must include the EVP for Finance or Treasurer. Domestic accounts need at least one additional finance division officer, and international accounts need two additional signatories.

query: Which benefits can employees continue through EBPA direct billing during an approved unpaid leave?
gold_answer: Medical, Dental, Optional Long-Term Disability, Optional Term Life Insurance and Dependent Life Insurance. Coverage terminates if payment is not received on time.
expected_policy: Benefits and Seniority Status While on Unpaid Leave of Absence

query: Under NYC traffic rules cited in the bicycle safety policy, when may a bicycle be ridden on a sidewalk?
gold_answer: Not unless a sign allows it, or the wheels are less than 26 inches in diameter and the rider is twelve or younger.
expected_policy: Bicycle Safety on the Morningside Campus

query: How much notice is required for blood donation leave?
gold_answer: At least three working days. Employees in essential roles, or where legal requirements apply and three days is insufficient, are expected to give ten working days' notice.

query: What must happen to air conditioners and refrigerators before they are discarded as bulk waste?
gold_answer: Facilities HVAC staff must remove the environmentally hazardous refrigerants (CFCs, freon) before disposal.

query: What does the Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy aim to protect against?
gold_answer: It sets acceptable methods for planning recovery of University business after loss of Key Business Systems, using a risk-based analysis.
expected_policy: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy

query: What are the SaaS and PaaS models described in the External Hosting Policy?
gold_answer: SaaS is a model where applications are hosted by a vendor and made available to customers over a network, typically the Internet. PaaS lets customers rent hardware, operating systems, storage and network capacity over the Internet to run or develop applications.

query: Why is an SSN required for tax reporting, according to the SSN Usage Policy appendix?
gold_answer: An SSN is required as the taxpayer ID for all tax information reported to the IRS, including wage and withholding data for faculty, staff and students, honoraria for guests, and payments to independent contractors.

query: What sample language can be added to a contract to evidence consent to electronic signatures?
gold_answer: The parties agree and consent to the use of electronic signatures solely for executing the Agreement or related transactional documents, and such signatures have the same full and binding effect as handwritten signatures.

query: Which unit bears overall responsibility for managing the University's DNS?
gold_answer: CUIT bears overall responsibility for managing the University's DNS, though it may delegate responsibility for certain internal and external domain names to other units.

query: Who is the exclusive catering provider to Lerner Hall and Faculty House?
gold_answer: University Event Management is the exclusive catering provider to Lerner Hall and Faculty House, with no exceptions except for religious reasons.

query: When must public performance rights for a film screening be secured?
gold_answer: Rights must be secured within 5 business days of the scheduled event. A license is required for any public setting on campus outside a student's residence hall room, whether or not admission is charged.

query: How many business days in advance must student events with furniture or Technical Services be cancelled in EMS?
gold_answer: They must be cancelled 5 business days in advance. Large scale performances or productions need 10 business days' notice.
expected_policy: Student Group Event Policy and Procedure

query: Who is responsible for ensuring occupancy limits are observed during an event?
gold_answer: The sponsoring organization must take positive actions to ensure occupancy limits are observed throughout the event, and ticket sales are restricted to the capacity limit.

query: Why does the Food Policy require food and beverages to be provided by a fully licensed and insured provider?
gold_answer: For health code and safety reasons, and to comply with the New York City Health Code and the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene's regulations.

query: Are food and drink permitted in classrooms used for non-instructional meetings?
gold_answer: No. Food and drink are not permitted in any classroom under the Non-Instructional Classroom Use Policy.

query: Which office administers the Gender-Based Misconduct Policy and the Interim Title IX Policy?
gold_answer: The Gender-Based Misconduct Office (GBMO) administers them in partnership with the Title IX Coordinator.
expected_policy: Gender-Based Misconduct and Interim Title IX Policies and Procedures for Students

query: Who decides whether directly charging office supplies and administrative expenses to a federal award is appropriate?
gold_answer: Only the Principal Investigator, using a facts and circumstances test that considers the needs of the science. If the costs were not budgeted, written approval from the funding agency is required first.
expected_policy: Charging Office Supplies and Other Administrative Expenses (Other than Salaries) to Federal Awards

query: What is the maximum duration of a special parking exemption on College Walk?
gold_answer: No more than one day. Longer parking must be requested from the Parking Office in a University parking facility.

query: How long is the grace period before tagged bikes in Commuter Bicycle Parking Enclosures are donated or discarded?
gold_answer: The grace period is 90 days after notification. After that, Environmental Stewardship will donate or discard the bicycles.
expected_policy: Commuter Bicycle Parking Enclosures on the Morningside Heights Campus

query: Can parents access a student's education records under FERPA at Columbia?
gold_answer: Only if the student is a dependent of the parents for federal income tax purposes. Otherwise records generally require the student's written consent unless FERPA permits release.
expected_policy: Federal Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)

query: What happens in Stage 3 of the commercial rent arrears process?
gold_answer: Commercial Real Estate conducts an internal review of the arrears report with commentary, submits it to CUFO Finance, and discusses critical issues in a monthly meeting.

query: Which federal regulations are the basis for the Compliance with Federal Cost Principles policy?
gold_answer: The Cost Principles in 2 CFR Chapter I and Chapter II Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles.

query: What does the policy on relationships with graduate students prohibit faculty from doing?
gold_answer: No faculty member may initiate or accept sexual or romantic advances or engage in a romantic or sexual relationship with a graduate student under the specified circumstances, because of the power differential.
expected_policy: Policy on Romantic and Sexual Relationships with Graduate Students

query: Why does Columbia treat undergraduates as particularly vulnerable under its romantic relationships policy?
gold_answer: Undergraduate students are particularly vulnerable to the power asymmetry of the student-teacher relationship, so the policy strengthened the earlier rule.
expected_policy: Policy on Romantic and Sexual Relationships with Undergraduate Students

query: Which office has overall responsibility for the University's anti-discrimination policies?
gold_answer: The Office of Institutional Equity (OIE), also designated as the Compliance Office for Title IX and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act.
expected_policy: Equal Employment Opportunity and Nondiscrimination Policies and Procedures

query: How quickly are most card access requests processed?
gold_answer: Most requests are processed within 1 business day, though cases needing additional authorization may take longer. The department administrator submits a service request through Public Safety ID Card Access.

query: What is the role of the Office of Record under the Procurement Records Retention Policy?
gold_answer: The Office of Record identifies the records to be retained and, in collaboration with OGC, determines the retention period. It also arranges proper storage, coordinating with outside vendors where appropriate.

query: How long must paper procurement documents also stored in the online system be retained?
gold_answer: They must be retained for a full year after the fiscal year in which the transaction occurred, unless a document hold or other exception applies.
expected_policy: Procurement Document Images as Document of Record

query: Which payees are exempt from the W-9 requirement?
gold_answer: University employees (including students receiving expense reimbursements), nonresident aliens and foreign entities, patient refunds, and petty cash reimbursements.

query: What law obliges the University to act on notices of copyright infringement by network users?
gold_answer: The 1998 Digital Millennium Copyright Act. For example, a notice from a record or film industry representative about illegal downloading requires the University to take action.
expected_policy: Copyright Information for Network Users Policy

query: How does the construction and repairs policy define a Project Request?
gold_answer: It is a request for a service or project outside normal routine maintenance and repair, usually done by an outside contractor with the cost charged to the requesting department.
expected_policy: Requests for Construction, Repairs and Maintenance

query: What is the maximum value an employee may accept from a lending institution in any twelve-month period?
gold_answer: Nothing of more than nominal value: $25 cumulatively in any twelve months, including cash, gifts, meals, travel, lodging and entertainment.
expected_policy: Conflict of Interest Policy Regarding Lending Institutions for All Employees

query: What must happen to a cost overrun with no expectation of sufficient sponsored funds?
gold_answer: The overrun must be transferred to a non-sponsored project upon discovery.

query: What kinds of cost sharing does the Cost Sharing policy distinguish?
gold_answer: Mandatory Cost Sharing (required by the sponsor), Voluntary Committed Cost Sharing (promised by the PI), and Voluntary Uncommitted Cost Sharing (neither required nor promised). Mandatory cost sharing needs a separate non-sponsored project.

query: What minimum value must an item have to be considered for leasing under the Capital Equipment Leasing Policy?
gold_answer: At least $50,000.

query: When is a Change Request required for a purchase order in CU Marketplace?
gold_answer: Payment amounts should match PO amounts within a tolerance set in the policy. Above that tolerance a Change Request is required.

query: At what contract value is a formal proposal process required in competitive procurement?
gold_answer: Contracts of $350,001 or more require a formal proposal process, with a cost or price analysis during bid review.

query: What security functionality must leased or purchased copiers and multi-function devices have?
gold_answer: They must include Hard Drive Data Wiping Software and a Data Overwrite Security System, which preferred vendor agreements provide.

query: Which federal regulations does the Procurement Mechanism Policy respond to?
gold_answer: Federal procurement laws and regulations including Uniform Guidance CFR 200.320 through 200.326 and the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR).

query: Which group is primarily responsible for capital equipment management at the University?
gold_answer: Capital Asset Accounting (CAA), whose Property Manager is the liaison to schools and departments. RPIC provides annual and final property reports for Government Owned/Furnished Equipment.

query: Who retains signature authority on goods and services contracts even when OGC leads negotiation?
gold_answer: The Purchasing Department performs the final review and retains signature authority.

query: What is a Purchase Requisition converted into after approvals?
gold_answer: A Purchase Order, in the University procurement system CU Marketplace.

query: How must restricted commodities needing prior approval be processed?
gold_answer: They must be processed through the Central Purchasing Office, are not covered by the Small Purchases policy, and require the correct category codes and chartfields in ARC for routing.

query: How should opportunities to bid be distributed among approved construction firms?
gold_answer: Routinely and equitably to all firms with a Task Order or Term Consultant Agreement, based on trade, specialty and project size.

query: What must appear on every invoice under Purchasing Terms and Conditions?
gold_answer: The order number and project number.

query: Below what value does University policy not decapitalize a true endowment, absent donor direction?
gold_answer: Not below 120% of the original gift value, adjusted annually at the HEPI rate (CPI before 1961), with adjustments beginning three years after the first gift.

query: What is the general single-transaction limit for P-cards?
gold_answer: Generally no more than $2,500 per transaction, along with a monthly credit limit.

query: When should change requests for central/current endowment status be submitted?
gold_answer: In July and August for the upcoming fiscal year, since attribute changes take effect at the start of the fiscal year. OMB has final approval of changes.

query: After how long may a student request removal of a disciplinary transcript notation?
gold_answer: At least one year after completing a Disciplinary Suspension or after a Withdrawal with Conduct Charges Pending. A student may make a total of two requests per notation.

query: Who is automatically considered a Delegate under the Rules of University Conduct?
gold_answer: All Deans and Deans of Students. Delegates have authority to enforce the Rules, warn violators and file complaints with the Rules Administrator.

query: What is the purpose of the Project Governance policy for capital construction projects?
gold_answer: To create a structure for clear and timely decision making in each phase so that late or changed decisions do not cause cost increases and construction delays.
expected_policy: Project Governance for Capital Construction Projects

query: What is the minimum age for receiving alcohol on the Medical Center campus?
gold_answer: 21. No one under 21 may be sold, served, given or otherwise receive alcohol, and no alcohol is served to a person who is disorderly or appears intoxicated.
expected_policy: Supplemental Guidelines and Procedures to Implement the University Policy on Alcohol at the Medical Center

query: How long may surviving spouses of officers of administration retain Columbia parking privileges?
gold_answer: Six months. Surviving spouses of officers of instruction, research and libraries retain them for three years in Columbia Housing or one year elsewhere.
expected_policy: Parking Policy for the Morningside Heights and Manhattanville Campuses

query: What disclaimer must accompany partisan political events held on campus?
gold_answer: That Columbia University does not support or oppose any political candidates, the views expressed are those of the speaker only, and the sponsoring group is sponsoring the event.
expected_policy: Partisan Political Campaign Activities on Campus or at Campus Facilities

query: Who pays for event insurance when an event is income-producing or sells tickets to the public?
gold_answer: The sponsoring organization bears the cost, if the University determines insurance is required.

query: How must the COLUMBIA name appear in event promotional materials?
gold_answer: It must be secondary to the event name, building name and street address, and all promotional material must be submitted before distribution.

query: Which offices must review the premise of a commercial shoot on campus?
gold_answer: The Offices of Communications and Public Affairs and the General Counsel. Production companies scouting locations are directed to the Executive Director of University Event Management.
expected_policy: Commercial Filming, News, Documentaries, and Student Filming Policy

query: What do searchers need to access the Housing Registry database?
gold_answer: A Columbia UNI and password. Searchers can create search profiles and get email notifications of matching listings.

query: Why does the site visits and audits policy require notification of sponsor reviews?
gold_answer: Sponsor reviews represent significant compliance risk and are in addition to the annual compliance audit under 2 CFR 200, so administrators must be notified.
expected_policy: Federal Agency and Other Sponsor Site Visits, Reviews and Audits

query: Which fire safety duty involves liaison with the New York City Fire Department?
gold_answer: Acting as liaison with the NYC Fire Department and other agencies involved in fire and life safety is one of the listed fire safety duties.
expected_policy: Fire Safety Policy and Procedures Morningside Campus

query: What peak heat release rate limit applies to single mattresses?
gold_answer: Not to exceed 100 kW, except in rooms protected throughout by sprinklers. Total energy in the first 10 minutes must not exceed 25 MJ.
expected_policy: Fire Safety Requirements for Upholstered Furniture and Furnishings

query: Who is 'authorized personnel' for restricted areas such as roofs and ledges?
gold_answer: University personnel who maintain, repair, secure or use materials in restricted areas, directly involved with equipment and systems, as designated by Facilities and Operations including Public Safety.
expected_policy: Roof, Ledge and Balcony Access - Morningside and Manhattanville

query: Which buildings does the lead-based paint policy focus on?
gold_answer: Residential buildings built before 1978, especially multi-family buildings where children under 6 are expected to live.
expected_policy: Lead-Based Paint Policy for Columbia Residential

query: What does the Locks and Keys policy aim to establish?
gold_answer: Rules for after-hours access, procedures for lost keys, lockouts, lock installation and repairs, and centralized distribution of keys.
expected_policy: Locks and Keys Morningside Heights Campus Academic and Administrative Buildings

query: Whom does the Financial Aid Code of Conduct govern?
gold_answer: Officers, employees and agents employed in a financial aid office or otherwise responsible for educational loans.

query: What does the CU Property Coordinator do?
gold_answer: Maintains asset records for CU-owned and government-owned equipment, tracks leases, keeps the tagging schedule, and oversees departmental equipment inventory verification required by federal regulation.
expected_policy: Management and Accounting for Movable Capital Equipment

query: How often is compliance of sponsored project expenditures validated?
gold_answer: Quarterly, annually and at project closeout.

query: What withholding applies to scholarship payments not used for tuition or required fees and books?
gold_answer: They are not a qualified scholarship and are subject to tax withholding of 30 percent or 14 percent depending on visa status, unless exempted by tax treaty.

query: May a Principal Investigator delegate day-to-day financial management of a grant?
gold_answer: Yes, but the PI must still exercise appropriate oversight of the project's overall finances, because the PI best understands scope, effort committed and relationships to other projects.
expected_policy: Principal Investigator Responsibilities for Financial Oversight of Sponsored Projects

query: Does Sponsored Projects Finance review individual transactions charged to grants?
gold_answer: No. It does not monitor individual transactions; appropriateness rests with the Principal Investigator and/or others with delegated responsibility.

query: Which expenses may never be charged to a federal grant or contract?
gold_answer: Specifically unallowable costs such as alcoholic beverages, entertainment, membership in non-professional organizations, and first and business class travel (coach or equivalent can be charged).

query: How are commencement expenses identified in ARC for F&A rate purposes?
gold_answer: They are unallowable for F&A rate calculation and are identified by the Initiative chartfield. Each school must establish an initiative to record them.

query: What must happen to records relevant to pending litigation, investigation or audit?
gold_answer: They must be retained until matters are resolved, appeals are exhausted and the retention period has expired, and all disposal of relevant records must cease.

query: How must relocation payments be processed effective January 1, 2027?
gold_answer: As additional compensation through Payroll using the REL earn code, not through Concur or by direct payment to a vendor.

query: Who has final authority over negotiating the Fringe Benefit and F&A rates?
gold_answer: The Executive Vice President for Finance, who assigned proposal development and negotiation to the Controller's Office.
expected_policy: Responsibility for Negotiation of Facilities and Administration and Fringe Benefit Rates

query: Are bulk mailings through Columbia Print allowed for personal purposes?
gold_answer: No. Mailings are for official Columbia business only, and requests go through the designated contact for approval before Columbia Print distributes.

query: When must a Business Associate Agreement be obtained?
gold_answer: Before PHI is disclosed to a business vendor, service provider or non-workforce individual that will create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI for CUHC. Workforce members may not disclose PHI without a fully executed BAA or other authorization.

query: What must riders do when boarding a University shuttle?
gold_answer: Tap their CUID/CUIMC ID on the card reader. Intercampus shuttles are free to employees and students, and there is no service on University holidays.

query: How should an overdraft in a restricted endowment or gift fund be relieved?
gold_answer: By moving expenses from the restricted fund to an unrestricted fund. Transfers from other restricted funds are not recommended because they complicate donor reporting.
expected_policy: Endowment and Gift Fund Administration and Compliance

query: May CUHC assign a code allowing de-identified information to be re-identified?
gold_answer: Yes, if the code is not derived from or related to information about the individual, cannot be translated to identify them, and is not used or disclosed for any other purpose.

query: What is a Hybrid Entity under HIPAA?
gold_answer: A single legal entity that is a Covered Entity, whose business includes both covered and non-covered functions, and that designates health care components within it.

query: How long does Ricoh copier delivery and installation generally take after a purchase order?
gold_answer: Generally 2 weeks.

query: What must service and recharge centers ensure about their billing rates?
gold_answer: That rates are adjusted periodically so costs recovered do not exceed actual costs of the goods or services provided.

query: Which laws does the HIPAA Breach Response and Reporting Policy respond to?
gold_answer: The HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR 164.400-414) and the New York SHIELD Act.
expected_policy: HIPAA Breach Response and Reporting Policy

query: Who coordinates monitoring of effort reporting forms in a department?
gold_answer: Department Chairs, Directors of Institutes and Centers, and/or Administrators, who also ensure salary adjustments are documented and cost transfers completed.
expected_policy: Charging and Documentation of Personnel Costs Charged to Sponsored Projects

query: How many sets of keys do residents in couples or family apartments receive?
gold_answer: Two sets, provided they completed applicable compliance procedures (students and postdoctoral fellows only).

query: When is rent due for students in Columbia Residential housing?
gold_answer: On the first of every month, billed by Student Financial Services. Late payment can lead to withheld registration, diplomas and transcripts or legal action.

query: What are acceptable reasons for a sponsored project cost transfer?
gold_answer: Correcting late information, reallocating effort to actual levels, fixing salary estimates, moving pre-award costs, allocating shared costs, correcting clerical errors, and removing unallowable or out-of-period charges.

query: When may the Health Plan disclose health information in legal proceedings?
gold_answer: In response to a court or tribunal order or a subpoena, only after reasonable efforts to notify the individual or to obtain a protective order.

query: What conditions make graduate coursework 'job-related' under the certification policy?
gold_answer: Either (a) it maintains or improves current job skills or (b) it is required to keep your job, and both (c) it is not needed for minimum job requirements and (d) it does not qualify you for a new trade or business or a doctoral degree.

query: What are the eligibility requirements for New York State Paid Family Leave at Columbia?
gold_answer: Employees must either regularly work 20 or more hours per week for at least 26 consecutive weeks, or work fewer than 20 hours per week and have worked at least 175 days.
expected_policy: New York State Paid Family Leave

query: Within how many business days does EBPA send a PTS scholarship check to the school after receiving a complete application?
gold_answer: Within 15 business days of receiving the completed application. Incomplete applications stay in 'Pending' status until all required information is received.

query: How often must CUHC workforce members complete HIPAA training?
gold_answer: When hired and annually thereafter. Those engaged in research must also complete the research-specific HIPAA course (RASCAL module TC0019).

query: Where is the Notice of Privacy Practices made available to patients?
gold_answer: It is given to every new patient and posted in faculty practice locations, describing patients' rights regarding their PHI.
expected_policy: HIPAA Privacy Rule and Patient Rights Policy

query: What does a HIPAA limited data set exclude, and what may it include?
gold_answer: It excludes direct identifiers such as names, street addresses, phone numbers, emails, SSNs, medical record numbers and full-face photographs. It may include town, city or state, gender and dates relating to the individual.
expected_policy: Limited Data Set and Data Use Agreement Policy

query: When may CUHC use PHI for marketing?
gold_answer: Not without the patient's authorization unless an exception permitted by law applies.

query: What does the Minimum Necessary Rule require?
gold_answer: Reasonable efforts to limit PHI accessed, used, disclosed or requested to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose.

query: What should staff record if a patient refuses to sign the Notice of Privacy Practices acknowledgment?
gold_answer: Indicate 'Patient refused to sign' on the form and document the staff name and the date the Notice was offered.

query: Who participates in the Sanctions Review under the Privacy and Information Security Sanction Policy?
gold_answer: The Chief Privacy Officer, Chief Human Resources Officer, Faculty Affairs or Student Dean and the department administrator as appropriate, with legal guidance from the Office of General Counsel.
expected_policy: Privacy and Information Security Sanction Policy

query: What protection does a person who files a privacy complaint have?
gold_answer: The Chief Privacy Officer ensures the individual is not retaliated against. Each complaint is promptly investigated and the individual receives a response on the outcome.

query: When does disclosing PHI for research not count as a Sale of PHI?
gold_answer: When the remuneration is only a reasonable, cost-based fee to cover preparing and transmitting the PHI.

query: Which kinds of platforms count as social media under the Social Media and HIPAA policy?
gold_answer: Blogs and micro-blogs, social networks, professional networks like LinkedIn, video and audio sharing, photo sharing, social bookmarking, public comment sections, and wikis.

query: What standard governs CUHC's requests for, use of, and disclosure of PHI?
gold_answer: Only as required or permitted by the Privacy Rule and consistent with the Notice of Privacy Practices, limited to the Minimum Necessary.
expected_policy: Use and Disclosure of Protected Health Information Policy

query: How many courses per term does the Tuition Exemption Benefit pay for Officers of Administration in degree programs?
gold_answer: Two courses per term, up to six per academic year, for undergraduate and master's programs at Columbia, Barnard and Teachers College.
expected_policy: Tuition Exemption Benefits For Officers and Family Members

query: Which collective bargaining units are covered by the support staff Tuition Exemption?
gold_answer: Local 1199/Morningside, Local 2110 UAW, Local 100, MEBA/MM&P/SSA (Medical Center), and TWU Local 241, along with non-union support staff who are actively at work and not on leave.
expected_policy: Tuition Exemption Benefits For Support Staff, Non-Union Support Staff, and Union Members

query: How many weeks of covered New York employment are needed for unemployment insurance eligibility?
gold_answer: 20 weeks within the 52 weeks prior to termination, among other conditions. The New York State Department of Labor determines entitlement.

query: What does the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act prohibit?
gold_answer: Paying anything of value to foreign officials to influence their acts or decisions or to secure an improper advantage in obtaining or retaining business.

query: Is consuming alcohol in an outdoor space without authorization allowed?
gold_answer: No. New York State law prohibits it, and outdoor events with alcohol also need outdoor space reservation authorization.
expected_policy: Columbia University Policy on Alcohol and Drugs

query: How many temporary schedule changes can eligible employees request under the NYC law?
gold_answer: Two temporary schedule changes per fiscal year for certain personal events, or one for two business days. Employees need 80+ hours a fiscal year and 120 days of employment.

query: At what rate is overtime paid to supporting staff scheduled for fewer than 35 hours?
gold_answer: One and one-half times the regular hourly rate, only for hours worked beyond 35 in the work week.

query: How often must non-union support staff receive written performance feedback?
gold_answer: At least once per year. The policy applies to Officers of Administration and Non-Union Support Staff.

query: Are contacts with federal grants officers by faculty seeking funding considered lobbying?
gold_answer: If the grants or contracts are awarded under a competitive review process, such contacts are not considered lobbying.

query: What is the relationship between the Statement of Ethical Conduct and other University policies?
gold_answer: It does not replace policies covering specific interactions; it provides a framework for them, with a basic set of expectations that is not comprehensive.
expected_policy: Statement of Ethical Conduct and the Administrative Code of Conduct

query: What happens to severance if a displaced employee accepts a temporary full-time benefits-eligible position of up to twelve months?
gold_answer: The severance allowance is suspended until the assignment concludes, after which the employee receives the severance agreed in the former position's separation agreement.

query: May employees use the University name to support or oppose a political candidate?
gold_answer: No. The University is prohibited by law from partisan political campaign activity, so employees may not use its name, facilities or property for or against any candidate.
expected_policy: Use of University Name, Facilities and Equipment

query: Which Public Safety resources exist for workplace violence concerns?
gold_answer: Emergency call boxes and Safe Havens throughout the area. Public Safety processes and investigates reports of criminal incidents.

query: What can reference checks verify about a prospective employee?
gold_answer: Dates of employment, job title, responsibilities and reason for leaving, plus the prior employer's view of the applicant's performance, accomplishments, strengths and weaknesses.

query: Are records not listed on the RRS-OTC covered by the Controller Records Retention Policy?
gold_answer: No. Any record not listed on the schedule, including records containing personal health information, is not covered.

query: When does supplemental compensation require written justification and VP approval?
gold_answer: When it exceeds 10 percent of base salary or $10,000 (whichever is less) during the year, it needs written justification and approval of the Vice President for Human Resources.

query: Who must approve pre-employment tests used to select employees?
gold_answer: Senior Human Resources Business Partners and the Office of Institutional Equity. Tests are valid only if they directly evaluate skills the applicant will use in the stated duties.

query: Why might an expatriate be seconded to an overseas entity?
gold_answer: To minimize the risk that the University is deemed to have a 'permanent establishment' in the foreign country, which could require filing tax returns and paying income taxes there.

query: May relatives work in the same work area at Columbia?
gold_answer: Not without prior written approval of the Vice President for Human Resources and Chief HR Officer, and no employee may work under direct or indirect supervision of an immediate family member without it.

query: Who must approve starting salaries above the hiring range?
gold_answer: The department's Senior Human Resources Business Partner.

query: How many personal days do full-time employees earn per year?
gold_answer: Up to three, earned at one day for each four-month period worked from the hire date. For officers and non-union support staff they do not accumulate and must be used within twelve months.

query: How many days of regular pay do non-full-time employees receive for jury duty?
gold_answer: Regular pay for scheduled hours missed, for a maximum of three days. Regular full-time employees are paid for the duration if the jury notice and court certification are provided.

query: May an Officer on paid medical leave relocate or travel extensively?
gold_answer: No. Officers are expected to remain at their primary residence, and plans to relocate or travel extensively may result in ineligibility for medical leave.
expected_policy: Medical Leave of Absence Full-Time Officers of Administration

query: What clearance is required before non-union support staff return from leave for a serious health condition?
gold_answer: Medical clearance from their healthcare provider, and the University may require additional clearance by a University-designated physician.
expected_policy: Medical Leave of Absence Non-Union Support Staff

query: In what circumstances may NYC employees use safe/sick time when a public official orders closure of their child's school?
gold_answer: When a public official orders closure or restriction of in-person operations at the child's school or child care provider due to a public health emergency or declared public disaster.
expected_policy: New York Safe and Sick Leave Policy

query: How much vacation do full-time regular Officers accrue with under 20 years of service?
gold_answer: 2 days per completed month of service, up to a maximum of 23 days; with 20 or more years it is 2 1/3 days per month up to 28 days.

query: How much paid time off may employees take to vote?
gold_answer: Up to two hours if they lack sufficient time outside work. Four consecutive hours before the shift or after it and before polls close counts as sufficient, and they must notify their supervisor two business days ahead.

query: When do weekly workers' compensation benefits begin?
gold_answer: After the seventh calendar day of absence.

query: What happens if SPA categorizes a subrecipient as 'high risk'?
gold_answer: SPA notifies RPIC, and together with the PI they decide whether a subaward should be issued, what special terms to include and what oversight is needed, mitigating risk before issuing it.

query: Which two groups share capital equipment management responsibility within the Controller's Office?
gold_answer: Capital Asset Accounting (CAA) and Research Policy & Indirect Cost (RPIC), so that both financial and government equipment rules are addressed.
expected_policy: Use and Maintenance of Moveable Capital Equipment

query: How long must Treasury retain tax-exempt bond issuance documents and records?
gold_answer: For the bond life plus 3 years. The Master Project List and annual certifications are retained 8 years.

query: Who coordinates the annual review of tax-exempt bond financed spaces for private business use?
gold_answer: The Office of the Treasurer, reviewing physical use of space, UBIT tax filings, leases, management and service contracts, and research agreements.
expected_policy: Post-Issuance Compliance Policy (Tax Exempt Bond Financings)

query: Why does the University retain records on tax-exempt bond financings?
gold_answer: To comply with the Internal Revenue Code and IRS regulations requiring conduit borrowers to support the bondholders' interest exemption, information filed on IRS returns, and reliance on arbitrage safe harbors.
expected_policy: Records Retention Policy - Tax Exempt Bond Financings

query: What is the departmental deductible under the Property Loss/Damage policy?
gold_answer: $10,000, the amount the impacted department is always responsible for.
expected_policy: Property LossDamage Reporting and Reimbursement Policy

query: Will OMB accept a budget that projects an operating overdraft?
gold_answer: No. All units should budget balanced or positive results, and units projecting a year-end overdraft must provide a plan to eliminate it.

query: Who can obtain CU Merchant IDs for accepting credit cards?
gold_answer: Only the Office of the Treasurer. Merchant environments must be validated by the CUIT-PCI Security Group before going live.
expected_policy: Credit Card Acceptance and Processing Policy

query: Is collision coverage mandatory for University vehicles?
gold_answer: It is mandatory for leased vehicles and optional for owned vehicles. Glass coverage has a $500 deductible.
expected_policy: Vehicle Acquisition, Operation and Disposal Policy

query: Who should be notified of a suspected violation of the Cash and Check Handling Policy?
gold_answer: The immediate supervisor, senior business officer, red flag program administrator, and the Associate Treasurer, Global Treasury Operations. The University Compliance Hotline is an alternative.

query: What is the maximum average outside consulting time for full-time faculty under the conflict of commitment policy?
gold_answer: An average of one day a week, provided it doesn't compromise University obligations.
expected_policy: Conflict of Interest Policy on Education, Clinical Care, and Administration for Faculty and Researchers at Columbia Univ

query: What are the purposes of the Capital Project Approval Process?
gold_answer: To provide consistent documentation of project proposals (purpose, scope, budget, funding, operating impact, schedule) and to establish appropriate levels of approval.

query: Which courses are excluded from the Reduced Employee Rate supplement?
gold_answer: Courses numbered with a 'Q' or 'N' (unless required for a degree), audited courses, and all doctoral courses.
expected_policy: Reduced Employee Rate Supplement to the Tuition Exemption Benefit for Officers Policy

query: What is Columbia's role under the Payments to Foreign Nationals policy?
gold_answer: Columbia acts as Withholding Agent, ensuring immigration compliance, proper tax withholding and preparing Form 1042 information returns.
expected_policy: Payments to Foreign Nationals and Entities

query: What happens if no dedicated lactation room is near an employee's work location?
gold_answer: The Office of Work/Life asks local HR or the Building Manager to identify a clean, functional alternative space other than a bathroom, which is then prioritized for lactation use with signage.

query: Whom should one notify if a minor is suspected abused by a Columbia community member and is not in immediate danger?
gold_answer: The Executive Director of the Office of the Protection of Minors, or report through the Office's reporting form. In immediate danger, call 911 and Public Safety.
expected_policy: Protection And Treatment of Minors at Columbia University

query: Are students responsible for emails sent to their official University address if they forward it elsewhere?
gold_answer: Yes. Students who redirect email do so at their own risk, and lost forwarded email does not absolve them of the obligations in those communications.

query: What must a P-Card cardholder do to return goods?
gold_answer: Contact the vendor directly and request a credit to the P-Card account. Cash or any other type of credit is prohibited.
